model.displayName: BERT Base NER — English Named Entities
model.description: A cased English BERT model fine-tuned on CoNLL-2003 news text and converted by Xenova for local browser inference. It extracts person, organization, location, and miscellaneous entity spans with confidence scores and character offsets.
intendedUses: Highlight named entities in English news-like text.
Prototype local document indexing, search annotation, and information-extraction workflows.
Provide candidate spans for human-reviewed downstream processing.
limitations: The model recognizes only PER, ORG, LOC, and MISC; dates, quantities, products, events, and other entity types are not represented consistently.
It was trained on English Reuters news from a limited historical period and may generalize poorly to other languages, domains, emerging names, informal spelling, or unusual capitalization.
Subword tokenization can split, truncate, merge, or omit entity spans; character offsets and labels require application-level review.
Confidence scores are not calibrated guarantees and must not be used alone for consequential decisions about people.
Inputs longer than 512 tokens are truncated, so entities beyond the retained prefix are omitted.

fixture.source: NASA Apollo 11 Mission Overview; lightly shortened without changing named entities.
fixture.preprocessing: Pinned cased BERT tokenizer with truncation at max_length; simple BIO aggregation.

benchmark.qualityGate: Finite in-range scores and valid ordered offsets; every checked NASA location/person span must be recovered with the expected label, exact normalized text, and score >= 0.8; output must be non-empty and non-degenerate.
benchmark.environment: Isolated headless Google Chrome on macOS; Transformers.js 4.2.0
